title: China's graft agency probes ex-Sinopec chairman Fu Chengyu
article:
(Oct 31): Fu Chengyu, the former chairman of China Petrochemical Corp (Sinopec), is under investigation for suspected serious violations of discipline and law, China’s top anti-graft agency said on Saturday.

Fu is undergoing a disciplinary review and supervisory investigation by the Central Commission for Discipline Inspection and the National Supervisory Commission, according to a statement on the agency’s website.

Fu Chengyu, born in 1951, is a veteran of China’s oil industry who led China National Offshore Oil Corporation before becoming the chairman and Communist Party chief of Sinopec in 2011. He departed Sinopec in May 2015 after reaching retirement age.

title: Bank of England may raise high-risk mortgage threshold, FT says
article:
(Oct 31): The Bank of England is considering easing restrictions on higher-risk mortgage loans in a move that could support the UK housing market, the Financial Times (FT) reported.

Under pressure from lenders and the government, the central bank’s Financial Policy Committee (FPC) is examining whether to increase a key lending threshold to five times borrowers’ household income, up from 4.5 times at present, the newspaper said. Since 2014, most banks have been prevented from offering more than 15% of mortgages to borrowers above that loan-to-income level.

The Bank of England told the FT that it “keeps its housing tools under regular review, having regard to the FPC’s primary and secondary objectives”.

According to the FT, the bank lobby group UK Finance estimates that raising the threshold could free up additional lending capacity equivalent to 7% of new residential mortgages.

The UK residential property market is under renewed pressure as surging mortgage costs squeeze prospective buyers. House prices stagnated in October, according to one of the country’s largest mortgage lenders, following a 0.3% decline in September.

UK Chancellor John Healey wrote to the Bank of England this week, urging the FPC to “target improving access to home ownership without prejudicing financial stability” and to consider how the loan-to-income threshold can better support that objective.

See also: Britain’s plan to tax its way out of debt tests the limits

That followed his move in Wednesday’s budget to double the UK’s bank tax surcharge to 6%, raising roughly £1.5 billion (US$2 billion or $2.6 billion) to help fund cost-of-living relief for cash-strapped households.

title: OpenAI’s Altman meets Samsung executives as chip crunch deepens
article:
(Oct 31): OpenAI chief executive officer Sam Altman met with Samsung Group’s top executives in South Korea on Saturday to deepen cooperation on memory chips and artificial intelligence (AI) infrastructure as global shortages intensify.

Samsung hosted Altman for talks with about 50 executives from its electronics, financial and biotechnology affiliates in Yongin, south of Seoul, the South Korean company said in a statement. The discussions focused on how AI can reshape industries, corporate decision-making and business opportunities over the next decade.

The meeting comes as shortages in a broad array of memory products strain the global electronics industry and send chip prices soaring. Demand from data-centre operators is intensifying competition for supplies, with the five biggest players in the AI infrastructure race planning to spend more than US$3 trillion ($3.8 trillion) in the coming years. Memory accounts for roughly a third of data-centre spending.

Altman is the latest American tech leader to visit South Korea, the leader in advanced memory chips and a country where AI adoption is accelerating among businesses and consumers. Nvidia Corp CEO Jensen Huang and Advanced Micro Devices Inc's Lisa Su both visited twice since last year to strengthen supply-chain ties. Technology executives have warned that chip production is struggling to keep pace with demand.

Saturday’s meeting builds on a partnership announced earlier to supply memory chips for OpenAI’s Stargate infrastructure project and cooperate on AI data centres, including floating offshore facilities. Samsung is also accelerating AI adoption across its businesses, from research and manufacturing to marketing and corporate operations.
